sections.content:
Welcome! 🎉 Every programmer on Earth started with this exact line. Python's **`print()`** function shows text on the screen.

Think of `print()` as Python *saying* something out loud. Whatever you put inside the quotes is what it says.

sections.label: Hit Run and watch what happens 👇

sections.content:
See that? The text inside the quotes showed up in the output box.

The quotes `' '` tell Python *“this is text”* (programmers call text a **string**). You can print anything you want!

sections.label: Try this one too
sections.code:
print('Python is awesome 🚀')
print('And I am learning it!')

sections.content: 💡 **Pro tip:** A line that starts with `#` is a **comment**. Python totally ignores it — it's a note for humans. Use them to leave yourself reminders.

sections.prompt: Your turn! Write a `print()` line that says **Hello, my name is** followed by a made-up name. For example: `Hello, my name is Alex!`
sections.starter: # Type your code below this line
hints: Use the print() function — just like the examples above.
Put your message inside quotes, like print('your text here').

check.description: Your program runs and prints a hello message with a made-up name in it.

tests.message: Print 'Hello, my name is' followed by a made-up name
